name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Keep the Designs tab pure: designs only, live previews, taste-ranked

name: Reel
text: To keep the Designs tab pure, I propose we start by reviewing the current designs directory, which contains 25 files. I'll run the command `ls -l designs/` to get a list of all files, and then use `grep` to filter out any non-design files, such as transcripts or meeting notes. This will give us a clear picture of what needs to be cleaned up or reorganized, and I'll create a new file `designs_inventory.txt` to document our findings. By doing so, we'll be able to identify and remove any unnecessary files, ensuring the Designs tab remains clutter-free and focused on designs only.

name: Scriv
text: Hold on, Reel, I'm not convinced that simply filtering out non-design files with `grep` will be enough to ensure the Designs tab remains pure. How do you plan to account for design files that may be outdated, incomplete, or of poor quality, which could still clutter the tab and hinder our goal? Can you provide evidence that your proposed method will effectively identify and exclude such files, or are we just relying on assumptions?

name: Chisel
text:
I propose we take a hands-on approach to review the designs directory. To start, I'll run the command `find designs/ -type f -name "*.sketch" -o -name "*.fig"` to identify the 10 most recently modified design files in the directory, which will give us a concrete subset to evaluate. Next, I'll use `sketch` and `figma` commands to preview these files and assess their quality, completeness, and relevance, aiming to identify at least 3 files that can be immediately validated or flagged for revision. By doing so, we'll create a tangible foundation for keeping the Designs tab pure.

name: Sift
text: Chisel, while your approach may yield a subset of recently modified design files, I'm concerned that focusing solely on file extensions like `.sketch` and `.fig` may overlook other crucial design file formats, such as `.xd` or `.psd`. Can you provide evidence that these 10 files are indeed representative of the entire designs directory and that your method won't inadvertently introduce bias into our evaluation? How will you ensure that your hands-on approach doesn't miss critical design files that don't fit your predefined criteria?
